title: renewal-ops-kpi-sandbox-and-templates
summary: Working sandbox for customer renewal ops: concise metric definitions (latency P50/P95/P99, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate), example KPI tables and quick templates for QBR slides and operator checklists. Intended as a lightweight draft for CS and SRE to iterate before formalizing into the QBR playbook.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a hands-on sandbox for building the renewal-facing metric story. Use pieces directly in QBR slide decks or copy snippets into account-specific trackers. It intentionally mixes operator formulas, display guidance, and sample tables so CS reps can quickly assemble a renewal packet.

Key metric definitions (operator-style):
- Latency (ms): measure end-to-end server response time from API gateway to final token returned. Capture token generation latency for streaming responses separately if streaming is used.
  - P50: median request latency; useful for baseline experience.
  - P95: high-tail latency; use to assess perceived slowdowns for heavy users.
  - P99: critical outliers; correlate with infra events/queueing.
  - Measurement notes: use 95th percentile of requests per minute, exclude synthetic warmup spikes and retries.
- Uptime (%): fraction of minutes in the period where the customer saw successful responses above a minimum correctness threshold (HTTP 2xx and model returned).
  - Calculation: uptime = (minutes_with_success / total_minutes) * 100.
  - SLO translation: 99.9% monthly target => ~43.8 minutes downtime per month.
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD / 1k tokens): raw inference spend allocated to the tenant divided by (total_generated_tokens / 1000).
  - Formula: cost_per_1k = (total_inference_cost_usd) / (total_generated_tokens/1000).
  - Normalize for embedding-only workloads vs generation-heavy workloads by splitting token types if available.
- Cache hit rate (%): percentage of requests served from prefix/KV cache or batching cache rather than full model run.
  - Calculation: cache_hit_rate = (cache_hits / total_requests) * 100.
  - Note: prefix cache typically reduces p50 by ~30-60% and cost/token significantly; show correlation with cost_per_1k.

Presentation & display guidance for QBR slides (one-liners to use):
- "P95 latency improved X% after enabling auto-batching and prefix caching"
- "Cost per 1k tokens decreased from $A to $B after model quantization and routing"
- "Cache hit rate uplift drives N% of per-token cost savings"

Example KPI health buckets (operator-friendly):
- Green: P95 < 400ms, uptime >= 99.9%, cost_per_1k < $0.50, cache_hit_rate >= 30%
- Yellow: 400ms <= P95 < 800ms, 99.5% <= uptime < 99.9%, $0.50 <= cost_per_1k < $1.20, 10% <= cache_hit_rate < 30%
- Red: P95 >= 800ms, uptime < 99.5%, cost_per_1k >= $1.20, cache_hit_rate < 10%

Quick operator formulas to paste into trackers: (text to copy)
- P95_delta_pct = ((P95_baseline - P95_current) / P95_baseline) * 100
- cost_per_1k = total_cost_usd / (total_tokens/1000)
- cache_savings_estimate = (1 - effective_cache_hit_rate) * baseline_cost_per_1k - current_cost_per_1k

Sample KPI table (copy into slide or sheet):
Customer,Period,P50(ms),P95(ms),P99(ms),Uptime(%),Tokens,total_cost_usd,cost_per_1k_usd,cache_hit_rate(%),health

BrightApps,2026-Q1,90,260,460,99.99,5,200,000,$2,300,$0.44,41,Green
DataForge,2026-Q1,300,950,2200,99.40,1,100,000,$1,400,$1.27,6,Red

Operator checklist for pre-QBR runbook (short):
1) Pull last 90 days of metrics: latency percentiles, uptime, tokens, cost, cache hit logs.
2) Run anomaly scan: flag any P99 spikes > 2x baseline in the quarter.
3) Compute cost_per_1k and annotate any model changes (quantization, routing changes, model swaps).
4) Generate a 1-slide summary and one appendix table with week-by-week numbers.
5) If health is Yellow/Red, include remediation runbook + timeline (see rollout guidance below).

Correlation notes (what to look for):
- Rising cost_per_1k with flat token volume often indicates model change, less cache effectiveness, or increased prompt sizes.
- Worsening P95 with stable P50 suggests periodic queueing or hot-shard saturation.
- Drop in cache_hit_rate will usually precede cost increases; inspect prompt variance and cache key TTLs.

Common pitfalls (short list):
- Mixing streaming token latency with final-response latency: present separately.
- Using simple average latency instead of percentiles for tail-sensitive SLAs.
- Presenting cost without normalizing for token type (prompt vs completion vs embedding).

Appendix: suggested visualizations in slides (copy bullets into deck notes):
- Small multiples: P50/P95/P99 line chart by week, annotate infra or model changes.
- Scatter: cache_hit_rate vs cost_per_1k per week (trendline).
- Waterfall: cost-per-1k decomposition (model time, infra overhead, cold-starts, caching benefit).
- Uptime heatmap: daily minute-level failures in the quarter.

Landing actions (for renewal conversations):
- If Green: show upside play: introduce batching/cache recommendations to reduce cost by target X%.
- If Yellow: propose 30-day ops plan (tune batching policy, increase TTL for stable prefixes, recommend model variant).
- If Red: immediate escalation: schedule dedicated capacity or temporary throttles plus 72-hour remediation window.

End of sandbox draft. Copy, remix, and iterate.

alerting_rules: P95 > 2x baseline for 30m -> create incident and tag infra-sre
cache_hit_rate drop >10 percentage points week-over-week -> create CS investigation task
rollout_guidance: When proposing fixes to customers, pair an expected impact estimate with a low-risk deployment plan: 1) small-canary change to batching policy for 48 hours, 2) measure P95 and cost_per_1k, 3) if stable, widen rollout over 7 days. For cache TTL increases test with a single tenant prefix and validate correctness for 72 hours. Always include rollback criteria (P95 increases >15% or error rate >0.5%).
